title: Review Generated Images and Content
subtitle: Learn to identify and evaluate AI-generated content for accuracy.
objectives: Identify images and content that are likely AI-generated.
Understand the importance of context and source for all digital content.
Evaluate information critically to avoid spreading misinformation.

scenes.title: Spotting the Fake
scenes.narration: Many online images look real but are not. It is vital to distinguish between real photos and generated content. Learning this difference helps us navigate online information.
scenes.visualAction: A cartoon character points to a screen showing a fantastical image, then looks puzzled.

scenes.title: What is Generated Content?
scenes.narration: Artificial Intelligence creates much online content. These generated items often look very realistic. Always check the source and context. Looking real does not mean it is true.
scenes.visualAction: A robot character draws an image on a tablet, then shows it to the viewer. Text bubbles appear: 'AI-made.'

scenes.title: The Moon Museum Poster
scenes.narration: Imagine seeing a poster for a 'Moon Museum.' It might look real. But what if AI made it for a story? Checking the source prevents misunderstanding.
scenes.visualAction: A cartoon character holds up an invented poster for 'Moon Museum opens tonight.' Another character points to a small label on the poster saying 'AI-generated illustration.'

scenes.title: Why Context Matters
scenes.narration: Always ask: 'Where did this come from?' and 'What's the real story?' Without context, AI images can be misunderstood. Critical thinking helps avoid misinformation.
scenes.visualAction: A magnifying glass icon appears over a screen displaying various images. Question marks float around the screen.

scenes.title: Adding Clear Labels
scenes.narration: Creators of AI content should add clear labels. These labels state if content is 'AI-generated' or 'fictional.' If sharing, add a label if it is missing.
scenes.visualAction: A cartoon character adds a label 'AI-generated' to an image on a digital canvas. Another character nods in approval.

scenes.title: Your Turn to Correct
scenes.narration: Now, practice! You will rewrite a misleading caption for an AI image. Clearly state it is illustrative and fictional. Check before sharing anything online.
scenes.visualAction: A character presents a tablet with an image and a caption. Another character begins typing on a keyboard.

scenes.title: Be a Media Detective
scenes.narration: Great job! You learned to identify AI content and its importance. Be a media detective: question, check sources, and be clear. Your critical thinking helps everyone.
scenes.visualAction: A character gives a thumbs-up. A thought bubble shows a checklist: 'Check source, Add label, Think critically.'

reading.title: Understanding Generated Content
reading.text: AI-generated content includes images, text, and audio created by Artificial Intelligence. These tools can produce highly realistic outputs. It's crucial to recognize that 'realistic' doesn't mean 'real.' Always assume content might be generated unless proven otherwise, especially if it lacks clear sourcing.

reading.title: The Importance of Context
reading.text: Context provides the background information needed to understand content correctly. An AI-generated image of a 'Moon Museum' is harmless in a fictional story, but misleading if presented as a real news announcement. Always seek out the original source and purpose of any content you encounter.

reading.title: How to Verify Content
reading.text: To verify content, look for official sources, check for 'AI-generated' labels, and consider if the information seems too good or too strange to be true. If you're unsure, avoid sharing it. When sharing content you know is AI-generated, always add a disclaimer.

materials.title: Invented Teaching Example: Context Label for a Generated Picture
materials.text: This example shows a context label designed to accompany an AI-generated image. The label reads: 'AI-Generated Content: This image of a fantastical floating island with waterfalls is a fictional illustration created by AI for a fantasy story. It does not depict a real place or event.' This label provides essential information about the image's origin and purpose, ensuring transparency.

promptExamples.initial: Create an image of a cat playing a guitar.
promptExamples.improved: Generate a realistic, high-resolution image of a tabby cat wearing a tiny fedora and strumming a miniature acoustic guitar on a small stage, with a spotlight shining on it. The image should be in a whimsical, artistic style.
promptExamples.followup: Can you make the cat look more like it's performing for an audience, maybe with a few cartoon mice cheering in the background?

activity.title: Caption Correction Challenge
activity.instructions: You've found an AI-generated image online with a misleading caption. Your task is to rewrite the caption to be accurate and transparent, clearly stating that the image is illustrative and fictional.
activity.starter: Image: A vibrant, detailed picture of a city made entirely of candy, with lollipop trees and chocolate rivers. Caption: 'New discovery! Scientists found a real candy land! So sweet!'
activity.expectedEvidence: A rewritten caption that correctly identifies the image as AI-generated and fictional, and explains its illustrative purpose.

quiz.question: You see a stunning image of a flying car on a news site. What's the first thing you should do?
options: Assume it's real because it looks good.
Check the source and look for 'AI-generated' labels.
quiz.explanation: Always check the source and look for labels before assuming an image is real, especially with advanced AI capabilities. Sharing without verification can spread misinformation.

quiz.question: Why is adding a label like 'AI-generated' important when sharing content?
options: It makes the content look more professional.
It helps prevent others from misunderstanding the content as real.
It's a requirement for all online posts.
quiz.explanation: Labels ensure transparency and help viewers understand the true nature of the content, preventing it from being mistaken for real news or events. It's a best practice for responsible sharing.

quiz.question: An AI-generated image of a historical event is used in a school project. What is the most responsible way to present it?
options: Present it as a real photograph from that time.
Use it as an illustration, clearly stating it's AI-generated and not a historical photo.
Claim it's a rare, newly discovered image.
quiz.explanation: While AI images can be illustrative, they must be clearly labeled as such, especially in an educational context, to avoid misrepresenting historical facts. Transparency is key.

mission.title: Create a Responsible Post
mission.instructions: Imagine you've used an AI tool to create an image for a fictional story about a future city. Now, you need to share this image online responsibly. Create a short social media post (2-3 sentences) that includes the image and a clear, transparent caption. The post should make it obvious that the image is not real.
rubric: The post includes a clear, invented image description.
The caption explicitly states the image is AI-generated or fictional.
The caption provides context for the image (e.g., 'for a story').
The post avoids any language that could mislead viewers into thinking the image is real.

hints.question: How can I tell if an image is AI-generated?
hints.answer: Look for unusual details, inconsistencies, or a lack of clear source information. Often, AI-generated images have a distinct 'look.' If you're unsure, assume it might be generated and check for labels.

hints.question: What kind of context should I provide for an AI image?
hints.answer: Explain the image's purpose. Is it for a story, a concept, or just an illustration? State clearly that it's not a real photo or event. For example, 'This is an AI-generated image for my sci-fi story.'

hints.question: What if I see an AI-generated image without a label?
hints.answer: If you are the one sharing it, add a label yourself. If someone else shared it, consider asking them for clarification or simply don't share it further until its authenticity and context are clear.

imageBrief.title: Context Label for AI-Generated Picture
imageBrief.scenario: A standalone digital label designed to accompany an AI-generated image online, providing essential context.
imageBrief.composition: A clean, rectangular digital card or box, with clear text. The card is simple, without a full image, but clearly indicates it's a label *for* an image.
labels: Text: 'Does not depict a real event'
imageBrief.altText: A digital context label card. The card clearly states: 'AI-Generated Content: This image is a fictional illustration created by AI and does not depict a real place or event. Used for creative storytelling.'

educatorNotes.sampleAnswer: For the activity: 'Image: A vibrant, detailed picture of a city made entirely of candy, with lollipop trees and chocolate rivers. Rewritten Caption: 'This amazing image of a candy city was created using AI for a fantasy story! It's a fictional illustration, not a real place.' For the mission: 'Just finished creating this AI-generated image for my new sci-fi story about a future city on Mars! What do you think of this concept art? #AIGenerated #FictionalStory #ConceptArt'
educatorNotes.commonMisconception: Students often assume that if an image looks realistic, it must be real, failing to recognize the sophisticated capabilities of AI generation. They might also believe that only 'bad' or 'fake' news uses AI images, not realizing AI is used for many purposes, including harmless creative ones.
reviewChecks: Does the student's rewritten caption explicitly state the image is AI-generated?
Does the caption clarify that the content is fictional or illustrative?
Is the tone of the caption neutral and informative, not misleading?
For the mission, does the social media post include a clear disclaimer about AI generation?
Does the mission post provide context for the AI image's purpose?
educatorNotes.safetyNotes: Remind students that while this lesson focuses on AI-generated images, the principles of checking sources and context apply to all online content. Encourage them to always involve a trusted adult if they encounter content that makes them feel uncomfortable or unsure.
